topic: Managing 40 client work permits in a shared Excel — what the first missed expiry actually costs
format: State the uncomfortable truth about how most Oman businesses handle this problem — be specific and honest, not preachy
post:
23 days of illegal work. One unopened spreadsheet.

Nobody caught it until the Ministry of Labour audit.

The company had 40 employees on work permits. All of them tracked in a shared Excel file. Colour-coded tabs. A designated person who hadn't opened it in two weeks — she was dealing with a payroll dispute and, honestly, who could blame her.

The fine hurt. But that wasn't the worst of it.

The worst part was having to sit across from a client and explain why their worker had been operating illegally for 23 days. That client relationship took 18 months to build. It didn't take 23 days to damage.

This is how work permit tracking actually breaks down in most Oman businesses. Not a system crash. Not a dramatic failure. Just a tab nobody refreshed.

When you're managing 10 permits, a spreadsheet works. At 40, you're not tracking permits anymore — you're hoping someone remembers to. Someone has to own every renewal. That same person has to be available, focused, and on top of it even when they're not.

That's the gap.
